coverage: Initial US official-source reference library; no local inspections or suitability guarantees

sources.name: Chipotle
sources.scope: US brand guidance; location and dish suitability unverified
sources.summary: The brand publishes an allergen matrix and special-diet notes. It warns that preparation cross-contact and test-menu exceptions can occur.

claims.note: Chipotle reports these are not ingredients in its standard food. This is not an allergen-free restaurant guarantee; limited-time or test products may differ.
Carnitas contains pork.

sources.name: Chick-fil-A
sources.scope: US brand guidance; location and dish suitability unverified
sources.summary: Ingredients vary with products, suppliers, and locations. Shared preparation areas prevent an allergen-free guarantee.

claims.note: Hand-breaded chicken is cooked in fully refined peanut oil. Keep this peanut-derived oil visible even when allergen-label rules exempt highly refined oils. TableRec makes no individual suitability determination.

sources.name: Five Guys
sources.scope: US brand guidance; location and dish suitability unverified
sources.summary: The official ingredient FAQ covers buns, frying oil, and equipment. Cross-contact remains possible.

claims.note: Fries use refined peanut oil; peanuts are also served in restaurants. The brand reports fryers used only for fries. Dedicated equipment does not establish personal suitability.
The published bun ingredient list includes wheat flour, milk, egg, soy-containing shortening, and sesame.

sources.name: McDonald’s
sources.scope: US brand guidance; location and dish suitability unverified
sources.summary: This record concerns US French Fries, not international recipes. Shared equipment and ingredient changes remain relevant.

claims.note: US fries list natural beef flavor with hydrolyzed wheat and milk starting ingredients. The product declares wheat and milk.
US fries include natural beef flavor; do not infer that they meet a vegetarian or vegan requirement.
McDonald’s USA does not certify or claim its US menu items meet halal, kosher, or other religious requirements.

sources.name: CAVA
sources.scope: US brand guidance; location and dish suitability unverified
sources.summary: Official nutrition and allergen guides are available. Supplier variation, shared preparation, and substitutions limit allergen and animal-product assurances.

sources.name: sweetgreen
sources.scope: US brand guidance; location and dish suitability unverified
sources.summary: The official guide requires choosing a location for item-level nutrition, allergens, and ingredients. A location selection is required before importing item claims.

sources.name: P.F. Chang’s
sources.scope: US brand guidance; location and dish suitability unverified
sources.summary: The takeout matrix covers allergens and additional sensitivities. Shared cooking prevents a no-cross-contact guarantee. Dine-in and takeout scopes must not be mixed.

claims.note: The separate gluten-free menu describes gluten-free ingredients and preparation procedures. It still asks guests to notify staff; this is not a celiac-safety certification.

sources.name: Panera Bread
sources.scope: US brand guidance; location and dish suitability unverified
sources.summary: The official page links US allergen and nutrition guides. Item and location scope must be checked; no individual dish claims have been imported.

sources.name: Jersey Mike’s
sources.scope: US brand guidance; location and dish suitability unverified
sources.summary: The brand warns that shared equipment, supplier changes, substitutions, and regional differences can affect allergen information. Item details require the current official tool.

sources.name: Red Robin
sources.scope: US brand guidance; location and dish suitability unverified
sources.summary: An official interactive menu supports allergen-based modifications. Staff describe an allergy-order kit and identification procedure; verify implementation locally.

claims.note: The FAQ cautions that steak fries may encounter allergens at the fryer station despite dedicated fryers. Dedicated fryer does not mean no cross-contact.

sources.name: Olive Garden
sources.scope: US brand guidance; location and dish suitability unverified
sources.summary: The brand describes allergy-order procedures and shared fryers. Its gluten-sensitive wording is distinct from a gluten-free certification.

claims.note: Shared fryers can introduce wheat/gluten, milk, soy, egg, and shellfish. Gluten-free pasta has separate handling; that does not certify every dish or the kitchen.

sources.name: First Watch
sources.scope: US brand guidance; location and dish suitability unverified
sources.summary: The brand warns about shared equipment, including a shared toaster, and asks guests to request its allergen-handling procedures.

claims.note: Highly refined soybean oil may not appear as a major-allergen flag. Preserve this oil information separately from the allergen chart.
Gluten-free products can be prepared on shared equipment. A gluten-free ingredient claim is not proof of celiac suitability.

sources.name: Cabo Bob’s
sources.scope: US official guidance; verify current location and dish details
sources.summary: The official FAQ discusses dietary choices and accommodations. Flour tortillas are made in the restaurant, so the environment is not gluten-free.

claims.note: Flour preparation can expose utensils and food pans to gluten. The brand describes glove changes and separately wrapped corn tortillas; local handling must be confirmed.
The brand lists dairy in buttermilk and smoky-cheddar tortillas, fried-fish breading, queso, cheese, sour cream, chipotle crema, and Ancho Rancho.
The FAQ identifies certain tortillas, beans, rice, vegetables, and sauces as vegan. This is a published option claim, not confirmation of every ingredient or kitchen practice.

sources.name: Picnik · Austin
sources.scope: Austin restaurant website guidance; verify the exact location and dish
sources.summary: The restaurant describes a menu without gluten or peanuts and lists avocado, coconut, and extra-virgin olive cooking oils. Treat these as restaurant claims, not independent inspection.

claims.note: The published menu claim is peanut-free and gluten-free. Individual kitchen verification, supplier details, and current cross-contact procedures are not established here.
The restaurant also describes grass-fed butter and honey in its approach. A peanut- or gluten-free menu does not make the entire menu dairy-free or vegan.

sources.name: Pita Pita · Illinois
sources.scope: Pita Pita Illinois business only; not Pita-Rita or Pita Pit
sources.summary: The restaurant publishes an HFSAA certification claim. This is a lead to verify with the certifier, not a checked certificate for every branch.

claims.note: Pita Pita states HFSAA certification. Certificate location, current validity, and scope must be verified; do not apply this to similarly named Pita-Rita or Pita Pit restaurants.

sources.name: H-E-B Kosher Deli · Austin
sources.scope: Specific Austin kosher deli; no chain-wide designation
sources.summary: The local Chabad resource describes the H-E-B kosher deli under Vaad Hakashrus of Austin supervision. This applies to the specified deli operation, not all H-E-B stores or all departments.

claims.note: Check the current certificate, exact counter, meat/dairy classification, and operating hours. No general H-E-B-wide kosher designation is made.

sources.name: CARVE American Grille · Barton Creek
sources.scope: 7415 SW Parkway, Barton Creek only; Central Austin temporarily closed
sources.summary: The location publishes vegetarian labels and a vegan modification for spaghetti squash primavera. Menu labels do not establish allergen absence or celiac suitability.

sources.name: Bouldin Creek Cafe · Austin
sources.summary: The cafe offers vegan dishes and vegan modifications, plus an official menu and linked allergy guide. Call the cafe about allergies; vegan labels do not establish allergy safety.
